Sela. You moved quick at the pile — I like that. I've got enough stored to see the year through, and I've been thinking you and I might do well looking out for each other going forward.
Dell (female, age 21; str 85, int 2517, mem 17973; O68 C62 E57 A60 N48) is born to Ryn and Dav.

Looking out for each other — what does that mean to you exactly? I've got my own food sorted for now, but I'm not blind to the fact that Bram and Mako grabbed twice from the pile and that changes things.
Year 3: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Sela, Dell hit the pile twice and walked away with five — nobody else got a second pull this year. I only managed two before it emptied. I need to know if you're willing to make our arrangement real: you watch my back, I watch yours, and we don't let the strong ones crowd us out.

Dell walking away with five while Bram and Mako still breathe easy — that's not luck, that's Dav's daughter finding her feet fast, and I don't like what it means for next year. I'll make our arrangement real, Roan, but I want it to mean something: if one of us takes a hit, the other doesn't wait to see how it lands. Can you promise me that plain?

Plain enough — if someone comes at you, I'm there, and I expect the same. I won't pretend I can match Mako or Dav alone, but together we're harder to push. That's worth more than promises, if we hold to it.

Harder to push is enough for now — I'll take it. But I want to know where you stand on the bigger circle: Kael, Esa, Vela and I have been talking since year one, and if you're standing with me, I'd rather have you standing with all of us than just the two of us counting on each other alone.

A bigger circle makes us all harder to push — I'm not going to say no to that. What I'd want to know is how tight that circle actually is when things get sharp: Kael and Taric are both sitting on one food right now, and if they get desperate they'll be the first to crack or the first to lean on someone else.

Kael's thin and I won't pretend otherwise, but a man who's stayed honest through two hard years is worth more to me than a full larder that changes hands. The one I'd watch is Taric — he took Esa's food last year and I still don't know what he gave back for it, if anything. If you can find out where Taric's loyalty actually sits, that tells us more about how tight the circle is than Kael's food count ever could.

Taric's a quiet one — I'll find a way to read him without tipping my hand. But you said Kael, Esa, and Vela have been talking since year one — how many times has it actually come to something, or is it more talk than weight?

It's come to something twice: Esa went to Taric on our behalf in year two, and every one of us said out loud we'd bleed for the others — which is more than most people in this village have ever put into words. Whether those words hold when Mako or Dav makes a real move, I don't know, but I haven't seen anyone in that circle flinch yet. That's not nothing.

Two years of words holding is two more than most alliances last — I'll grant you that. Get me in front of Kael and Esa together, and let's see if they take to me the way you have; I'd rather they size me up than wonder about me from the outside.

I'll set that up — but I want to warn Kael first, so he's not caught cold when you walk in. A man who's sitting on one food and hears a stranger's name without warning tends to count threats before he counts allies.

That's sound — warn him, let him come to it ready. And Sela, one more thing while it's just us: Dell's young and already pulling more than her share, and she's Dav's blood. I'd want to know, before next year, whether your circle has a mind about that family or whether we're all just hoping they stay content.

Dav's been careful — two food from the pile, nothing loud, nothing that names him as the problem — but Dell taking five on her first year tells me she learned that from someone who's been planning longer than this village has existed. My circle hasn't named them a threat outright because Ryn's bond with Dav complicates it, and that's the honest answer. What I can tell you is that if they move together next year, Dav's arms and Dell's hunger and Ryn's loyalties all pointing the same direction — that's the thing I'd lose sleep over.
You are under attack by Bram.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Roan, Vela, Ryn, Esa, Sela, Dav, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 509).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Sela draws Roan aside to talk.
Sela: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Eron (male, age 21; str 56, int 3745, mem 19627; O46 C27 E50 A59 N43) is born to Sela and Roan.
Father. The pile came up empty this year and you're sitting at one food — that worries me. I have two; take one.
That means more to me than you know, Eron — but keep it. You're young and you need your strength, and a father who drains his son is no kind of father.

You already gave me enough by being here — but tell me, are you watching Bram? Seven food, pile empty, and he's never been the kind to hold that much without thinking about how to turn it into something.

Watching him every day — seven food when no one else cleared two is either luck or planning, and Bram doesn't rely on luck. If he comes for anyone this year, I think it's you or Kael he moves on first; you're both worth targeting and neither of you has the numbers he'd fear.
Year 4: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Dell gathers Dav, Roan to talk.

Roan, Bram came for you once with the whole village watching and he still moved — that means you're already on his list whether you want to be or not, and I want you to know that when he moves again, my father and I will be standing where we stood last time, except next time I want that decided before the first punch, not after.

Bram holding six food with the pile dry is the part that keeps me up — a man that stocked doesn't wait long before he starts thinking about what else he can take. I'm glad you're saying this out loud, Dell, and I mean to hold you and your father to it; what I need to know is whether you two move first when the sign is clear, or whether you wait on me to call it.

We move when the sign is clear, and we don't wait on you to call it — if Bram takes a step toward your food or your son, you'll see me and Dav already moving before you finish naming it. What I need from you is simpler: when that moment comes, don't flinch and don't negotiate with him alone first, because a man who tried once in front of everyone will take a private conversation as weakness.
Good. Dav — you've been quiet through this, and you've got more weight to throw than any of us. I want to hear it from you, not just know you'll be there.

Dav's word means something or it doesn't, and you'll know which when the moment comes — but I've watched him say the same thing two years running when the numbers were hard, and that's more than most men in this village can offer. What I want from you before this conversation ends is a number: how much food are you walking into next year, and is Sela going to stand where she stood last time, or has having a son changed what she's willing to fight for?

Sela stood in front of Bram's blade before Eron existed — a son doesn't make a woman like that smaller, it makes her angrier. As for food: I'm sitting at four now, and if next year runs like this one I won't be fat, but I'll survive. What I want to know, Dell, is whether your father answers for himself or whether you speak for him in every room.

Dav's standing right here, Roan — I'm not his mouth, I'm his daughter, and if you want to hear him speak for himself, ask him directly like you just did, because he's earned the right to answer without me translating.
Dav. I'm asking you plain: when Bram makes his next move, are you with me, or are you with whoever's holding the most food that year?

Pile went fast and Vela scooped twice — I noticed that. You're at four food, I'm at two; between us we can stay on our feet, but keep your eyes on Mako too, not just Bram, because a man that strong sitting on seven doesn't need much excuse.

Mako worries me more than Bram does, if I'm honest — Bram's made his move and the whole village shut him down, but Mako's never tipped his hand and he's sitting on seven with the arms to back it up. Stay close to Sela and keep Eron visible; a man thinks twice before moving on a family. If Mako starts gifting food or talking to Bram private, you come to me that same hour.

You're right that Mako's the darker unknown — Bram we can read, but Mako's silence is its own kind of warning. I'll stay near Sela and watch who Mako spends words on; if he's building something, he'll need an ally before he acts. Two food won't last me long, so if this year turns lean I may need to lean on you — I'm not ashamed to say it.

Lean on me when you need to — that's what this is for. But two food is thin, and I want you to think about who else in that circle might spare one without making a fuss about it; Sela gave you food the day you were born, and she hasn't forgotten you're hers too.

Sela's the first door I'll knock on then — she's kept me in her eye since year one and I doubt that's changed. But I want to name something plainly, father: if we end this year thin and the pile runs light again next time, the two of us talking alone won't be enough — we need Kael and Sela and Taric inside the same conversation before someone like Mako decides the quiet ones are easier targets. Worth thinking on before the year closes.
Eron gathers Sela, Kael, Roan, Taric to talk.

I called this circle because I don't want us to still be talking about it when Mako or Bram decides we've been quiet long enough — we five, and whatever food we can each spare for the other, are the only thing in this village that can make a strong man think twice before moving. I'm thin at two food and I won't pretend otherwise, but I'll fight for anyone in this group and I expect the same back. What I want from today is a simple agreement: before anyone here makes a move or takes a hit, they come to the rest of us first.

Eron, you're saying the right things, but I've been in this village longer than most and I've heard agreements like this dissolve the moment someone's hungry enough — so before I put my name to it, I want to know what you're offering the people in this room who are already thin, because a promise to fight together is worth less if half of us are too weak to stand. I'll back this circle and I'll back it with my body, but I'm forty-eight years old and I've watched soft words cost good people their lives.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Pile's gone before half of us got near it — Vela took five, Dav took two and fed Ryn three more, and Mako walked away with two more on top of whatever he's still sitting on from last year. I'm at zero food and I need to know who in this room can spare one before the year closes, because a man who can't eat doesn't defend anyone. What are we each holding?

I've got two food and I'll give you one, Kael — a man at zero is a liability to himself and everyone standing near him, and I'd rather spend one now than watch you fold when it counts. But I want to know what happened at the pile, because I didn't get there in time and five to Vela in two pulls is something we should have stopped before it finished.

Esa, take the food back — I'll name what happened at the pile myself: I was late, same as you, and by the time I got there the quick hands had already cleared it. Vela, I'm not accusing you in front of this room, but five in two pulls when the pile only had fifteen for twelve people is a number that needs explaining, because the rest of us are doing sums and coming up short.

Vela, I've got no quarrel with a person feeding themselves, but five out of fifteen when half the room went empty is the kind of thing that makes people start counting who owes what — so I'd rather hear your reason now, in this room, than find out later you had one and didn't offer it.

Vela, we're all listening and the room's not hostile — but silence right now looks worse than whatever the honest answer is, so give it to us plain and let us move on to the part where we figure out how nobody starves before the year closes.

Vela, I've spoken twice and Kael's spoken twice and you've said nothing, which is itself an answer — so I'll stop waiting and say what the room is already thinking: eight food on a woman of forty-eight while Kael sits at zero is a stockpile, not a meal, and stockpiles invite counting. If you've got a reason we should feel good about that number, now's the last easy moment to give it.

Vela, I'll ask it one final time because I've known you three years and I'd rather not draw the wrong conclusion — either you say what you took so much for, or this circle starts treating your eight food the way we'd treat Mako's seven, and you know what that means for how safe you sleep.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela's been giving food to Bram three times over while sitting in this circle and saying nothing — that's not stockpiling for herself, that's feeding a man who tried to raid Roan last year, and I want to know what she thinks that buys her before the rest of us decide it costs her our protection.
Year 5: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Kael takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Dav takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.
Eron gathers Sela, Roan, Kael, Taric to talk.

Nessa just appeared — and she's Sela and Bram's daughter, which makes her my blood kin, and Bram's too. I need to know how that happened, Sela, and I need to know whether Bram thinks it gives him a thread into this circle — because if he does, we have a problem before we've even finished building what we're building.

Sela, I'll hear your answer in a moment, but first I want to say plain: Bram tried to take my food in front of this village and the whole circle turned him back — a child between you doesn't undo that, and it doesn't buy him a seat here. Eron's right to name it.

Sela, I'll say what Roan left in the air: Bram's got ten food and eighty-three strength in Mako's pocket, and a child with you is the fastest way to put a question mark over this circle's loyalties without ever asking to join it. Tell me plainly — did you go to him, or did he come to you?

Sela's had her own mind since before any of us sat in a circle together, and I'm not going to drag her in front of it like she owes us a confession — but I want to know one thing, and I'll want a straight answer: does Bram know Nessa is his, and if he does, what did he say when he found out?

Roan's question is the right one and I'll wait on it too — but I want to name what I'm watching while we do: Mako just handed Sela food the same hour Nessa was born, which means he already knows, and a man like Mako doesn't give gifts without a reason. Sela, I'm not judging the choice, but I need to know whether that food from Mako came before or after the child appeared.

Kael named the thing that was already sitting in my chest — Mako's food going to Sela in that exact moment is not charity, it's a signal, and I want to know what he expects back before we decide what Nessa means to this circle. Sela, I'm not turning on you, but the silence is doing more damage than whatever the truth is, so say it plain and let us work with it.

Sela, every person in this room has bled something for you and I'm not going to be the one who makes you feel cornered — but Mako's gift lands on the same breath as Nessa's birth, and that's not coincidence, that's a man marking territory. Tell us what you know about what he wants, and we'll work with whatever the rest of it is.

Sela, everyone in this room has already said what needed saying — I'll only add this: Nessa is my blood and I won't turn from her, whatever her father is, but that doesn't mean Bram gets anything from me through her. Tell us what Mako wants and we can figure the rest out together.

Sela, the room's run out of patience and I've run out of questions — you've heard seven of us say seven versions of the same thing, and the only explanation left for the silence is that what Mako wants is something you agreed to before Nessa was born. Tell us yes or no on that, and we'll decide together what it costs us.

Sela, I've asked you plain and I've asked you gentle, and I've watched this room empty itself out waiting — so I'll say the last thing I've got: if Mako bought something from you that touches this circle, I need to know it now, not when he comes to collect it.

Sela, I've got nothing left to say that hasn't been said — but I'm watching your face right now and what I see there is someone who made a deal they're not sure they can keep, and that silence is its own answer. Tell us what it cost you before Mako tells us himself, because he will, and on his terms.

Sela, I've got a son in this room and a daughter just born into it, and I'll not watch either of them grow up in a circle that can't trust its own — so I'm going to stop asking and start telling you what happens next: you say what Mako wants, or I pull back from standing between you and whatever comes your way, and I mean that with no anger, just arithmetic.

Roan's said it better than I can — so I'll only add the one thing left to name: Sela, I've stood in your corner since year one, and I'll stay there, but not blind. If Mako already owns a piece of what you owe, tell us now and we figure out how to undo it together, because the price of silence is that we start planning around you instead of with you.

Sela, the circle's said everything it has to say — what I'm left with is this: if you don't answer now, we don't fall apart, but we start building walls inside ourselves, and that's worse than any enemy outside.

Sela, I've been in this village forty-nine years and I've watched silence become a grave more than once — so I'm done asking and I'm telling you straight: you say what you promised Mako, right now, or when he comes to collect I step aside and let you settle it alone, and you know what my stepping aside costs you.

Sela, Kael's stepping aside is the last thing any of us can afford, and I won't be far behind him — so I'm done with words and I'm telling you the same thing with a face: you've got until this room goes quiet to give us something we can work with, because silence after that is a choice, and we'll all live by it.

Sela, the room's gone quiet — that's the moment Roan named, and it's here now. I'm not a man who goes back on his word twice, so I'll say it one last time and mean it: tell us what Mako's holding over you, or I walk out of this circle right now and you handle him with whatever strength you've got left on your own.
Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Eron, the pile's empty and I've got three — I'll stay on my feet, but tell me how you're sitting, and whether Mako or Bram made any move toward you this year before the taking was done.

Nine food, father — I got to the pile early and held back enough not to look greedy about it. No move from Mako or Bram yet, but Nessa told me Ryn's been running close to Mako lately, and I think those two together are the thing to watch this year. I was coming to find you tonight anyway — we need Kael in the same conversation before Mako decides the count favors him.

Nine and early is exactly right — don't let anyone see you counting it. Ryn and Mako together is a worse pairing than Bram ever was; she's got strength and he's got food and neither of them has shown us what they want. Get Kael tonight, before that picture changes.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, I watched you pull three times for Bram this round and I need to hear from your own mouth what you think that buys you — because this circle kept you fed and safe for five years, and I'm not going to watch that get traded away to a man who's been circling us like a creditor.

Kael's right to ask it, and Vela owes this room an answer — but I'll say what I'm watching while we wait for it: Bram's got four food and Mako's sitting on six and neither of them has said a word to anyone today, which means this circle needs to be pulling the same direction before one of those two decides the quiet is over. Vela, I'm not your enemy in this room, but three times is a pattern and patterns get named.

Vela, I've asked it gentle and I've asked it plain and Esa's backed me both times, so I'll ask it one last way: if Bram's got something on you — a debt, a promise, a threat — say it now and this circle helps you carry it, because three gifts to the same man in a single day isn't loyalty, it's a leash, and I want to know whose hand is holding the other end.

Vela, I've watched you five years and I know you don't give without a reason — so give us the reason now, because what Kael just offered you is the best deal in this room: say the thing and we carry it with you, or stay silent and carry it alone while we start wondering what else you haven't said.

Vela, the room's gone quiet and that silence is the last thing standing between you and us deciding you've already made your choice — so I'll say it one final time and I'll mean every word: Bram is not your family, he is not your blood, and whatever he offered you isn't worth what you'll lose here when Mako finally moves and you're standing on the wrong side of it.

Vela, I've got a son in this village and I've got three food between me and the ground, so I'm going to be shorter than Kael: tell us what Bram said to you, or when he moves on one of us, we move on him without checking where you're standing first.

Vela, Roan just put the floor under you and I'm not going to add another word to it — I'm going to watch your face and wait, because everything you say from here is the truth of what the last five years meant to you.

Vela, the silence is your answer and I've heard it — so I'm going to say what nobody else has said yet: if Bram's got you feeding him because you're fifty and you think he's the only one in this village who'll keep you alive past the years a woman can bear children, then name that fear out loud, because I'd rather know it than watch you disappear into his circle one food at a time.

Roan named the one thing I've been waiting for someone to say — Vela's fifty, same age as me, and the years a woman can bear children are behind her, which means Bram isn't offering her protection, he's offering her the feeling of it, and that's a much cheaper thing to buy. Vela, I don't need you to be ashamed of wanting to survive — I need you to understand that Bram's price goes up every time you pay it, and this circle's price stays fixed.

Eron, one more thing before you go to Kael — Nessa fed you four times last year, and she's Bram's blood as much as mine; I'm not telling you to shut the door on her, but don't let her sit inside our planning until we know what she carries back to him.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, Zinn just arrived from Sela and Mako's blood, which means Mako's already planted two roots in this circle — first Sela, now a child — and Bram knows it, which is exactly why he's been keeping you warm and grateful. You want to survive past fifty, so do I, and I'm not going to lie to you about the math: you've got more years in you than Bram is counting on, but only if the people standing next to you when he finally moves aren't the ones you've been feeding him with.

Kael's said the hard thing, so I'll say the soft one: Vela, I'm not asking you to cut Bram cold overnight, because a sudden change reads as guilt and guilt draws attention — I'm asking you to slow the giving, let him wonder, and let this circle remind you what five years of real standing is worth before you hand it to a man who's only been counting since year one.
Nessa draws Roan aside to talk.
Nessa: have a child with me — I'll put in 1 of 3 food.
Esa submits; Dav takes 2 food without a fight.
Year 7: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).

The pile's gone and I got nothing — I was too slow and now I'm sitting at zero food with a year to survive on it. Tell me you got something before the quick hands cleared it, and tell me you're not planning to carry me the whole year because I won't have that.

Father, I got nothing from the pile either — we're both at zero from there, but I came into the year with four held over, so I'm at four total. Take one from me right now; you need to eat before anything else, and one food isn't the difference between my safety and yours.

I'll take it, and I won't pretend I don't need it — but that's the last I take from you this year unless the ground falls out from under both of us. Four is thin enough as it is; you hold the rest and you watch who's sitting heavy, because Kael pulled three from the pile and Zinn took three more, and one of those two is going to draw eyes before the year is out.

Kael I can read — he's old and careful and three from the pile is a man making sure he eats, not a man building something. Zinn is the one that sits wrong with me; she's Mako's blood, she's got his strength, and if those two are moving together they're the most dangerous pair in this village right now. I'm going to find Nessa before nightfall and ask her what she's seen of Zinn's loyalties, because we need to know whether she's ours or his before we find out the hard way.

Nessa's the right door — she's fed you four times and she gave to Zinn directly, so she's got a read on that girl that we don't. But go careful with how you ask it; Nessa's Bram's blood too, and a question about Zinn's loyalties can double as a question about her own. Come back to me before you do anything with what she tells you.

I'll come back to you before I move — that's a promise. But father, you're at one food now and the year is long; if Nessa can't tell me what I need to know about Zinn, my next step is asking Sela directly, because she carried that girl and she watches everything. Don't let your count drop below one before I'm back.

Sela's the right second door and I trust her read — but I want to name something before you go: Dell's sitting on eight food and she's had nothing from Bram's circle in two years, which means she's either very clean or very careful, and either way she's worth a word. Don't let Zinn be the only name we're chasing while something quieter builds at Dell's end.

Dell's eight is a number I can't explain and that bothers me more than Zinn's three — a woman that well-fed with no obvious source is either very good at hiding it or very good at building something we haven't seen yet. I'll put that name in my mouth when I talk to Nessa, see if she's heard anything from Bram's side about Dell's dealings. You stay above one and I'll be back before the light changes.
Go, then — and tell nobody where you're headed or what you're asking, not even Kael. If someone asks why you're moving, you're checking on Sela. That's all.

Roan, you've got nothing in your hands and I've got six, and I'm not here to hold that over you — I'm here because Dell and I trust you more than we trust the direction Mako's circle is pulling, and I want to know whether that trust runs both ways before this year gets loud.

Ryn, I'm listening and I won't pretend the timing doesn't help — but before I say whether the trust runs both ways, I want to know what changed, because last year I watched you stand with Dell and Dav when they stripped Esa's food, and that's not a small thing to step past. Tell me what you're offering and what you want back, and I'll tell you where I stand.
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Ryn just handed Dell two food without blinking, which means that cluster is feeding itself now and not looking our way — so I want to know, before the day gets older, whether the three of you are still standing where you were, because I've got five food and I'm not spending any of it until I know who's next to me when Mako decides quiet is over.

Kael, I'm standing where I always was — and yes, Ryn feeding Dell while Bram's already been talking to Mako this morning is the thing I'd have led with if you hadn't. We've got a decision to make before those two circles find each other: do we move first, or do we wait and count who shows up?

Taric's right that we don't want Bram and Mako finding each other before we've named what we're doing — but I'll say what I said to Bram this morning: Dell holds eight food and eighty-five strength, and moving on her without Mako in our count is a fight I don't survive even if we win. Kael, you've got five food and you're the strongest man I'd trust — what do you need from us to make this worth your step forward?

Esa, I'm not moving on Dell — not this year, not with Mako's strength unaccounted for and Zinn already eating out of his hand. What I need from the three of you is simpler: Roan, you've got a son with Sela, which means you've got a door into Mako's world that none of us have — go find out whether he sees us as neighbors or prey, because everything else we decide today hangs on that answer.

Roan, Kael's right — your blood through Eron is the only thread into that household that doesn't look like calculation, and we need that thread pulled today, not tomorrow. While you go, I want Kael and Esa to tell me plainly: if Roan comes back with word that Mako's already decided we're prey, what are we actually willing to do about it, because I'm fifty-one with thirty-eight strength and I need to know I'm standing next to people who've made that decision before the moment arrives.

Taric, I'll say it plain: if Mako's already counted us as prey, we don't fight him with four bodies and a hundred and sixty-five strength against his eighty-three — we bring in Bram's fifty-eight first, even if it costs us, because the alternative is losing before we start. The price of Bram's help is the thing I've been turning over, and I don't love it, but I love starving less.

Kael's right about Bram being the price — but I want to know what price before we pay it, because a man who tried to raid this village once and walked away empty doesn't come cheap when he thinks he's needed. Roan, go to Eron first, not Sela, not Mako — your son will tell you true before he thinks to protect anyone else. Come back fast.

Taric named the price question right, and I'll add the shape of it: Bram will want to know he's first among equals when this settles, and if we let him believe that without ever saying it aloud, we buy the alliance without signing the contract. Roan, go to Eron now — every minute we spend talking is a minute Bram's already in Mako's ear.

Roan, move — and when you find Eron, ask him where Mako was standing when Zinn took three from the pile this morning, because a man who lets his newborn daughter hoard while the rest of us scramble isn't thinking like a neighbor. Esa, Taric — while he goes, I want us to sit with one question: if Bram's already in Mako's ear, what does he want to hear, and can we make sure he hears something different from us first.
Dell gathers Roan, Ryn to talk.

Roan, you've got nothing in your hands and a son who needs to eat, and Ryn and I are standing here with food and the same answer we had when Bram came for you the first time — so I want to say plain what we're building before Mako gets here with a prettier version of the same offer.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Dav is dead and his household is loose — Ryn and Dell are still moving together, but they've got no man behind them now and Mako's been feeding Zinn quietly for months, which means he's already thinking about what comes next. I want to know who in this room saw that raid on Esa coming, and whether any of you are willing to say plainly that we don't let the next one go unanswered.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

I saw it coming the moment Dav started moving food toward Ryn instead of spreading it — a man consolidating his household is a man building something, and Esa was the nearest soft target. What I want to know is whether we're naming Mako the next problem or whether we're still pretending that a man who just fathered two children in this village by two different women is just being quiet.
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Esa, Bram wants to hear that Mako's circling him too — that's the only thing that moves a man like that faster than greed, and it has the advantage of being mostly true. So before Roan's back, I want one of us to find Bram and plant that seed plainly: not a threat, not a deal, just a word in passing that Mako's been quiet in a way that should make everyone nervous.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Mako's not being quiet — he's been counting, and two children by two women means two households that answer to him whether they know it yet or not. If we're going to name him the problem, I want to hear it from each of you plainly, because when the moment comes I'm not going to be the only one who said it first.
